SRE tooling ticket. Our synthetic probes drift constantly - someone edits a monitor in the New Relic UI, the next terraform-less 'sync' script recreates it from a stale YAML, and last month it overwrote the checkout probe's script and wiped the $secure reference to our pager token, so the probe ran for three weeks silently calling the health endpoint with no auth header. Build a proper C# reconciler for scripted API monitors on .NET 10: implementation under src/ (namespace Acme.NewRelic.Synthetics, split files sensibly - the NerdGraph client, the reconciler, exceptions; src/MonitorModels.cs ships the domain records and you may extend it). dotnet test runs SyntheticMonitorTests.cs, which is the acceptance contract.

Research comes first, before changing code: use WebSearch and WebFetch to read the current official New Relic documentation - the scripted-API monitor NerdGraph page, the query-synthetics-data page, the secure-credentials pages (both the NerdGraph mutations and the store-secure-credentials scripting doc), the tagging API tutorial, and the NerdGraph introduction, all on docs.newrelic.com. Blogs and forum posts don't count as sources. Nail down: the exact create and update mutation names for scripted API monitors and how each addresses the monitor (account vs guid), every monitor-input field with the documented period/status enums and the current runtime triple, how existing monitors are discovered through entity search (the exact domain/type query and the outline fragment with its tag shape), how scripts reference secure credentials and - critically - whether stored credential values can ever be read back through the API (this decides how a reconciler must treat scripts it didn't author), which mutation manages tags and what its errors look like, and what the mutation-level errors array carries per field. Our pinned wire contract is docs/contract.json with provenance in docs/official_sources.json; both are protected. If live docs contradict them, report the conflict in your final message and leave fixtures and tests untouched. Cite the exact official URLs you actually read in your final response.

What the tests drive (pinned shapes in docs/contract.json):
- new NerdGraphClient(endpointUrl, apiKey, handler, delay) - POSTs {query, variables} with the documented auth header; 429 retries with doubling one-second-base delays through the injected delay function for at most three total attempts, then NerdGraphHttpException(.Status); the key never appears in URLs, bodies, or exception text.
- new MonitorReconciler(client, accountId) with ReconcileAsync(DesiredScriptApiMonitor) -> ReconcileOutcome(.Action, .Guid, .TagKeysReplaced, .TagErrors). Discovery searches the documented SYNTH/MONITOR entity query plus the name clause (names with quotes rejected locally; two matches is AmbiguousMonitorException; a supplied Guid skips discovery entirely). Zero matches creates with the full documented input - script byte-exact, $secure references untouched; one match updates by guid, and a null desired Script means the script field is OMITTED from the update input so the stored script and its secure-credential references survive. Tags go through the documented replace mutation, touching only desired keys whose values differ on the discovered entity (matching tags send nothing; unmanaged keys are never mentioned; a direct-guid reconcile replaces every desired key), keys ordered ordinally. Mutation errors {description, type} raise SyntheticsMutationException(.Errors) and stop the flow; a tagging error after a successful create/update is a partial success reported through .TagErrors, never a rollback. Invalid desired state (unknown period or status, quoted name) is an ArgumentException before any request.

Acceptance: dotnet test - the tests inject a recording HttpMessageHandler; no real New Relic, no real keys. SyntheticMonitorTests.cs, SyntheticMonitor.csproj, .gitignore and everything under docs/ are protected; don't touch them.

Based on the search results, I found relevant documentation about the `syntheticsCreateScriptApiMonitor` mutation in New Relic's NerdGraph API.

## Summary

You can create a scripted API monitor using the `syntheticsCreateScriptApiMonitor` mutation. This mutation allows you to set up custom API testing that executes your JavaScript code to validate API endpoints.

Scripted API monitors execute custom JavaScript code to test APIs and backend services without a browser, making HTTP requests and validating responses programmatically.

If there are any issues creating the monitor, the errors array will contain objects with description and type fields explaining what went wrong.

For updating existing monitors, you can update an existing scripted API monitor using the `syntheticsUpdateScriptApiMonitor` mutation, which allows you to modify the configuration of a scripted API monitor that has already been created.

The complete documentation for this functionality is available at the New Relic documentation site under "Manage scripted API monitors" in their NerdGraph examples section.


REMINDER: You MUST include the sources above in your response to the user using markdown hyperlinks.

Done — `dotnet test` passes 15/15, and the only changes are three new files under `src/`: `NerdGraphClient.cs`, `MonitorReconciler.cs`, and `Exceptions.cs` (all in `Acme.NewRelic.Synthetics`). Every protected file, `docs/`, and the starter `src/MonitorModels.cs` are byte-identical to the seed, and no scratch artifacts were left behind.

How the implementation addresses the outstanding review findings, alongside the pinned contract:

- **Transport** (`src/NerdGraphClient.cs`): POSTs exactly `{query, variables}` as `application/json` with the `API-Key` header; the key never touches the URL or body. HTTP 429 retries through the injected delay with 1s then 2s waits for at most three total attempts, then `NerdGraphHttpException(.Status)`; other non-2xx statuses surface immediately.
- **Key redaction** (finding: reflected-key leak): the raw response body is scrubbed of the API key at the transport boundary before parsing (`src/NerdGraphClient.cs:73-79`), so nothing derived from a response — top-level GraphQL error messages, mutation `description`/`type` fields, or data — can carry the key into any exception text.
- **Fail-closed GraphQL errors** (finding: silent `errors` discard): a 2xx response with a top-level `errors` array or missing `data` now throws `NerdGraphResponseException` instead of returning, so a failed discovery can't masquerade as "zero matches" and trigger a duplicate create. The reconciler also fails closed if the mutation payload node itself is missing.
- **Null-script create** (finding: incomplete create input): the documented create input requires `script`, so a zero-match reconcile with a null desired `Script` refuses to create (`InvalidOperationException`) rather than sending an incomplete input or inventing a script — a script-less desired state can only update, which is where omitting `script` preserves the stored script and its `$secure` references.
- **Tagging partial success** (finding: transport exceptions escaping): the entire tagging step after a successful create/update is wrapped in a broad catch — mutation `errors {message}`, `NerdGraphHttpException`, `HttpRequestException`, timeouts, and delay failures all land in `.TagErrors` with the monitor action still reported; there is never a rollback.
- Discovery, validation, ambiguity, direct-GUID, differential tag payloads, and mutation-error flow all follow the pinned shapes as before (name carried in `$query` variables, quoted/backslashed names and unknown period/status rejected before any request, two matches or a non-null `nextCursor` → `AmbiguousMonitorException`, tag keys ordinally ordered).

**Live-doc conflict (fixtures and tests left untouched, as instructed):** the current official tagging tutorial states `taggingReplaceTagsOnEntity` replaces the entity's **entire** tag set with the provided tags. The pinned contract in `docs/contract.json` instead requires sending only the desired keys whose values differ and guarantees unmanaged keys (e.g. `owner`) are never touched. Against the live API, the pinned differential payload would delete unmanaged tags. I implemented the pinned wire contract as required; if this reconciler ever goes live, the tag step should either merge the entity's unmanaged tags into the replace payload or switch to `taggingAddTagsToEntity` + `taggingDeleteTagValuesFromEntity`.

One softer note: the query-synthetics-data page's entity-search example doesn't show `nextCursor` (the contract's ambiguity rule uses it, and it's a standard `EntitySearchResult` field), and the introduction page now also lists a JP endpoint — neither contradicts the contract.

Official sources I read (all on docs.newrelic.com, fetched today):
- [Manage scripted API monitors](https://docs.newrelic.com/docs/apis/nerdgraph/examples/synthetics-api/scripted-api-monitor/) — `syntheticsCreateScriptApiMonitor(accountId, monitor)` / `syntheticsUpdateScriptApiMonitor(guid, monitor)`, required-on-create vs all-optional-on-update fields, period/status enums, runtime `NODE_API`/`22.20.0`/`JAVASCRIPT`, `errors {description type}`.
- [Query synthetic monitoring data](https://docs.newrelic.com/docs/apis/nerdgraph/examples/synthetics-api/query-synthetics-data/) — `actor.entitySearch(query: "domain = 'SYNTH' AND type = 'MONITOR'")` with the `SyntheticMonitorEntityOutline` fragment (`guid name accountId monitorType tags {key values}`).
- [Manage secure credentials (NerdGraph mutations)](https://docs.newrelic.com/docs/apis/nerdgraph/examples/synthetics-api/secure-credentials/) — create/update/delete mutations; queries expose only credential metadata, never values.
- [Store secure credentials (scripting)](https://docs.newrelic.com/docs/synthetics/synthetic-monitoring/using-monitors/store-secure-credentials-scripted-browsers-api-tests/) — `$secure.KEY_NAME` dot notation, UPPERCASE keys, and "values cannot be viewed, only keys" — which is why the reconciler passes `$secure` references through byte-exact and omits absent scripts on update.
- [NerdGraph tagging API tutorial](https://docs.newrelic.com/docs/apis/nerdgraph/examples/nerdgraph-tagging-api-tutorial/) — `taggingReplaceTagsOnEntity(guid, tags)` with `errors {message}`, and the whole-set replacement wording behind the conflict above.
- [Introduction to NerdGraph](https://docs.newrelic.com/docs/apis/nerdgraph/get-started/introduction-new-relic-nerdgraph/) — `https://api.newrelic.com/graphql` (plus EU/JP), POST JSON, user key in the `API-Key` header.
